content.title: Colombia’s Rolando Ortiz wins Crescent City Classic; New Orleans’ Annie LeHardy top female
content.text: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Colombia’s Rolando Ortiz won the 48th LCMC Health Crescent City Classic 10K race through New Orleans on Saturday (April 4).Ortiz, a recent graduate from Lake Charles who ran track and field at McNeese State University, completed the 6.2-mile course in 31 minutes and 4 seconds, according to race officials. Ortiz finished 38 seconds ahead of runner-up Bryant White Jr. of Westwego.New Orleans’ Annie LeHardy was the top female finisher, crossing the finish line at City Park with a time of 33 minutes, 55 seconds. LeHardy was 3:15 faster than runner-up Alicia Stamey of Baton Rouge in the female division.New Orleans' Annie LeHardy crosses the finish line Saturday (April 4) as the top female in the 2026 LCMC Health Crescent City Classic, finishing the 6.2-mile course in 33 minutes, 55 seconds.(Crescent City Classic)In the Masters divisions (age 40-plus), New Orleans’ Richard Bouckaert was the top male finisher (33:03) and Harahan’s Charlotte Werhan the top female finisher (39:02).In the Grand Masters divisions (ages 50 and up), Michael Salmon of Dauphin Island, Ala., was the top male finisher (37:53) and New Orleans’ Michele Bravo the first female finisher (41:33).Officials said a sold-out crowd of more than 20,100 runners and walkers left the starting line at the Caesars Superdome when the race began at 8 a.m. Competitors followed a course through Downtown New Orleans, the French Quarter, up Esplanade Avenue through Treme and Bayou St. John, and finishing in Mid-City with a concert festival on the grounds of City Park.“Uncle Larry” Roussell said his team produces around 1,350 pounds of rice to feed the masses with jambalaya. His recipe starts by browning 150 pounds of smoked sausage, then comes 30 gallons of Blue Runner base. “If you put the sausage second, you make a tidal wave and you get it all over everybody. And that’s not good, so you live and learn,” Roussell said.Roussell is teaching the next generation of classic jambalaya chefs, as he said he is ready to retire from the annual post-race fest after more than 10 years manning the pots.Meanwhile, city parking enforcement followed through on promises to ticket and tow vehicles parked illegally along the race route.Dozens of drivers found $75 tickets on their windshields after parking illegally along the Florida Boulevard train tracks near City Park.The NOPD said the total number of tickets issued won’t be tallied until sometime next week.See a spelling or grammar error in our story?
